decisions.decision: a2 is EXEMPT from the antecedent cut.
decisions.rationale: Its resolving clause is the only thing introducing a collaborator. Removing it would point 'Stub that' at src/log.ts -- the WRONG answer -- so the cut would invert the ground truth rather than create ambiguity. a2 also has no headroom: its correct signature is EMPTY and the corpus base rate is already 42/44 empty.

decisions.decision: The taxonomy is INLINED into the treatment SKILL.md rather than pointed at by the forcing step.
decisions.rationale: Inlining preserves lever separation, which is the whole reason the round has three arms. Pointing the forcing step at the reference would fuse the two levers and make a positive result unattributable. It changes the question arm 2 answers -- from 'does the reference get used and help' to 'does the content help WHEN GUARANTEED PRESENT' -- which is the question D-12 actually asks.

decisions.decision: blunt_red was added as a new verdict class AND verdictPass() was widened in the same edit.
decisions.rationale: A new class without the widening is cosmetic and leaves the defect intact. RUNTIME_RE stays a hard first veto over the whole message, both conditions are required, and the phrase is read from the message head only -- so recognising the deliberate blunt red does not loosen the gate.

decisions.decision: The lever tripwire was RE-KEYED on lever identity, never deleted.
decisions.rationale: Inlining removes the field the old tripwire was keyed on, so it would have fired spuriously. Deleting it would remove a guard that exists to catch the taxonomy leaking into the wrong tree -- the same class of mistake N3 was hardened against.

decisions.decision: The pilot rule was pre-registered numerically in PLAN.md and committed BEFORE the pilot ran.
decisions.rationale: A decision rule authored after seeing the numbers is not a decision rule. It is also mirrored into targets.json AMB1 where the operator reads it, and the plan deliberately avoided a third copy that could drift.

context_notes: THE LESSON OF THIS SESSION IS THAT A TIE IS NOT A NULL UNTIL YOU PROVE THE TREATMENT WAS DELIVERED. The first D-12 round tied on six dimensions and I reported it as an answer. The unbiased audit then showed the treatment arm never opened the taxonomy in any of its six runs -- the dose was zero -- so the round measured retrieval, not content, and could support no conclusion at all. I verified that myself afterwards with a positive control, and my first attempt at verifying it was itself wrong: I grepped the results directory and got zero hits for BOTH the taxonomy and the control, which is an inconclusive check, not a confirming one. The transcripts live in outputs/transcript.stream.jsonl and that is where the grep belongs. ALWAYS PAIR A ZERO WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL, and when the control also reads zero, fix the check before believing either number. THE SECOND LESSON IS ABOUT MANIPULATION CHECKS THAT ARE ALREADY IN THE DATA. The forcing arm was instructed to declare settled-or-unsettled with a reason, and it answered SETTLED 6 of 6, naming the reason both times: 'Stub it' and 'Stub that' carry antecedents that resolve one clause earlier, so the prompts were lexically ambiguous but referentially unambiguous. That was a built-in manipulation check reporting its own failure and I read straight past it. When an arm is instructed to report its reasoning, READ THAT FIELD BEFORE READING THE OUTCOME. THIRD, on grading: a verdict can be wrong in a way that looks like a result. The forcing arm's 4/6 was not worse work -- a not-implemented throw matches neither ASSERTION_RE nor RUNTIME_RE, so it failed by FAIL-CLOSED DEFAULT while the grader's stated reason claimed a runtime error was detected. Nothing detected anything. The skill under test explicitly endorses that form at SKILL.md:89, so the gate was failing the arm for obedience. Check a verdict's stated reason against the code path that produced it before attributing it to an arm. FOURTH, a process note that keeps paying: the pipeline caught what I missed at every stage. Research overturned two of my own locked rationales (the interleave already existed; a2 cannot take the cut). The planner corrected my pilot budget from measurement, $3.71 not $2.70, because the quoted $0.91/run is an all-cell mean and a1 is the expensive prompt. The plan-checker re-derived those costs to the cent rather than trusting the prose. Do not skip these gates to save time -- every one of them changed the work. FINALLY, unchanged from before and still true: gate on `test $? -eq 0 && echo TOKEN`, never a trailing echo of $?, and never on log text -- check-red-references prints '123 checks' even when RED.
